scoringComposition.defect: no per-dimension floor exists anywhere — only the summed total is compared against the threshold
scoringComposition.workedExample: for a standard component at threshold 90: a perfect Pass 1 scores 70 with zero sighted input. Craft then needs only 20 of 30. Maxing the three minor craft dimensions (7+5+3=15) and scoring defaultVisualQuality at 5 of 15 — visually ordinary by any normal reading — reaches exactly 90 and is dispositioned 'accepted'. The one dimension that asks whether it looks good is 15% of the total, while the fully automated pass is 70%.
scoringComposition.reviewGate: review status/reviewer/timestamp/notes are checked only as non-empty strings, with no linkage to the numeric scores

freshness.searchResult: zero hits for sourceDigest / artifactSha256 / sha256 / digest across the v1 modules
freshness.liveProofOfDrift: the repository's own shipped scorecard.example.json FAILS its own validator today — it is missing a required evidence key that registry.mjs demands. Nothing catches it, because the wired command only runs validate-manifest and never validate-scorecard.
freshness.wiring: quality-evidence:check appears in package.json but in no CI workflow, no gates:ci, no pretest and no lint — it is genuinely advisory, exactly as the R0 defect list claimed

v2Design.separationLaw: binary eligibility and the 100-point sighted craft score are computed by SEPARATE modules. craft-score.mjs never receives a contract result, so a green gate cannot raise a sighted score; eligibility.mjs consumes the score only to compare it against the family's layer threshold.
modules: contracts.mjs — loads and resolves the nine-file contract pack
craft-score.mjs — weighted sighted score with evidence-required and applicable-weight renormalization
eligibility.mjs — binary verdict: contracts, vetoes, taxonomy, stress floor, divergence, restore, receipts, completion contract
receipts.mjs — freshness by artifact sha256 and source digest, non-vacuity, producer-is-not-approver
admission.mjs — work-order admission enforced before write, plus conflict-graph safety
round-evidence.mjs — per-round minimum evidence policy, roundLayout allowlist, status-key law, SHA256SUMS freshness
seal-round.mjs — generated-only SUMMARY.json and the SHA256SUMS seal

gateReachability.trapFound: `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` is a NON-RECURSIVE shell glob, so a drill file placed inside scripts/quality-evidence/v2/ would never run under the umbrella suite
gateReachability.whyItMatters: a gate nobody runs is not a gate. The round's own exit criterion is that the evidence policy is enforced rather than advisory — shipping 29 drills that the umbrella cannot reach would have reproduced the exact v1 defect being fixed.
resolution: added a named script `quality-evidence:v2:drills`, matching the existing per-gate precedent in this package
extended `test:scripts` with an explicit second glob so the drills run under the umbrella too
gateReachability.creditedTo: the read-only tooling scout, which found the trap empirically rather than assuming the glob was recursive

showroomRegistryDrift.note: the showroom registry is a PROJECTION of the inventory, not an authority. Its drift is recorded for Codex, not fixed in this round.
showroomRegistryDrift.onboardingSwapConfirmed: the registry lists OnboardingSurface as an experience surface. OnboardingSurface is real but is a sub-component inside the forms/wizard family, so the registry displays a non-family sub-component in place of the genuine ninth experience family, which is entirely absent.

coverage.denominatorBasis: the five layers the registry covers at all — primitive 100 + pattern 56 + chart 18 + structure 27 + surface 36. surface-composition (4) and commercial (11) have no registry file and are excluded from this ratio rather than counted as misses.
coverage.countingRule: each registry row's `name` is resolved against family-inventory.json by family name, then by membership in a family's `components` array. A row that resolves to no family covers nothing; two rows resolving to the same family cover one.
coverage.reproduction: node -e with family-inventory.json indexed by family name and by component, parsing `slug`/`name` pairs out of the five registry files; prints rawRows, distinct covered, double-coverage pairs and unmatched rows
coverage.correctionOfAnEarlierNumber: an earlier draft of this receipt claimed 218 of 237. That number came from subtracting two known-bad rows from the raw count under an UNSTATED rule, which is precisely the failure this program names: a number is not evidence until its scope is stated. The verified figure is 216, because there are FOUR defective rows, not two.

fourDefectiveRows.detail: resolves to primitive/feedback/modal, which primitives modal:Modal already covers — the registry reintroduces OverlayModal-as-its-own-family without spelling the name

OnboardingSurface is a component INSIDE surface/forms/wizard, which surfaces wizard:WizardSurface already covers. It is additionally filed under the wrong group (experience rather than forms), which is why the genuine ninth experience family reads as present when it is absent.
no `PageShell` export exists. The canonical pattern family is PatternPageShell; PageShellSurface is a different layer (surface-composition) and is outside this denominator.
no `Record` export exists. The real owner structures/record/content exports RecordSummaryStrip, RecordFieldGrid, RecordField, RecordActionBar and RecordPanel.

showroomRegistryDrift.arithmetic: 220 raw − 2 rows naming no export = 218 rows that resolve; − 2 double-coverage collapses = 216 distinct families.
showroomRegistryDrift.misnamingIsWhyTwoFamiliesReadAsMissing: PatternPageShell and RecordContent appear in the missing list precisely BECAUSE their registry rows are misnamed. The showroom still generates a page from each slug, so those two families are reachable but mislabelled — not invisible. Stated so nobody reads the 21 as 21 absent pages.
